'''Maureen Elizabeth Downey''' (May 1, 1921 – May 14, 2000) was an American [[Zoology|zoologist]] who worked for three decades at the [[Smithsonian Institution|Smithsonian]] [[National Museum of Natural History]]. Known as "The Starfish Lady," she was an authority on [[Starfish|sea stars]] and other [[echinoderm]]s, co-founding the International Echinoderm Conference in 1972. Among her discoveries is ''[[Midgardia xandaros]]'', the world's largest starfish.

== Early life and education ==

Maureen Downey was born in [[Washington, D.C.]], in 1921.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Pawson|first=David L.|date=2000|title="The starfish lady", Maureen Elizabeth Downey, 1921-2000|work=The Echinoderm Newsletter|issue=25|url=http://www.marinespecies.org/echinodermfiles/enl/ENL_25.pdf|access-date=2021-05-03}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Miscellaneous San Juan County, WA Obituaries|url=http://www.obitcentral.com/obitsearch/obits/wa/wa-sanjuan1.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040919014238/http://www.obitcentral.com/obitsearch/obits/wa/wa-sanjuan1.htm|url-status=usurped|archive-date=September 19, 2004|access-date=2021-05-03|website=Obitcentral}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|date=2000-05-31|title=Obituaries|language=en-US|newspaper=Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/2000/05/31/obituaries/876d035c-d266-4cec-ab56-3e33e85d9825/|access-date=2021-05-03|issn=0190-8286}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Maureen E. Downey (1921-2000)|url=https://www.gulfbase.org/people/maureen-e-downey-1921-2000|access-date=2021-05-03|website=GulfBase}}</ref> She had an early fascination with animal biology, bringing insect specimens to be identified at the [[National Museum of Natural History]].<ref name=":0" />

She studied at [[George Washington University]], then [[Duke University]] and the [[University of Washington]]'s [[Friday Harbor Laboratories]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

== Career ==

Downey was an international authority on echinoderms, particularly sea stars, earning her the nickname "The Starfish Lady."<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> While she occasionally studied other groups, such as [[brittle star]]s, her work primarily focused on sea stars.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Singletary|first=Robert L.|title=A New Species of Brittle Star from Florida|date=1973|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/24319456|journal=Florida Scientist|volume=36|issue=2/4|pages=175–178|jstor=24319456|issn=0098-4590}}</ref> Her work with echinoderms began in the 1940s, when she worked briefly at the [[Duke University Marine Laboratory]] in [[North Carolina]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

She began her career in Washington, D.C., serving as a civil servant at the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] and later at the [[United States Fish and Wildlife Service]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> In 1957, she joined the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History as a secretary. Over time, she transitioned to a museum technician role, focusing on echinoderms. Her dedication and expertise led to a promotion to museum specialist, where she conducted research on starfish and improved the accessibility of the museum's echinoderm collection. She also authored two comprehensive catalogs, covering [[echinoids]] and [[ophiuroids]] found in major collections throughout North America, during her 30-year tenure at the museum.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

In 1967, she co-founded the ''Echinoderm Newsletter'', and in 1972 she co-organized the first International Echinoderm Conference at the National Museum of Natural History.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ziegler|first1=Alexander|last2=Mirantsev|first2=Georgy V.|last3=Jangoux|first3=Michel|last4=Kroh|first4=Andreas|date=2014-03-28|title=Historical aspects of meetings, publication series, and digital resources dedicated to echinoderms|url=https://zse.pensoft.net/article/1090/|journal=Zoosystematics and Evolution|language=en|volume=90|issue=1|pages=45–56|doi=10.3897/zse.90.7201|issn=1860-0743|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ziegler|first1=Alexander|last2=Kroh|first2=Andreas|date=2012|title=Echinoderm conferences and symposia: a concise history and bibliography|url=https://www.mapress.com/zoosymposia/content/2012/v7/f/v007p001-024.pdf|journal=Zoosymposia|volume=7|pages=1–24|doi=10.11646/zoosymposia.7.1.2}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=David|first1=Bruno|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AzoLEAAAQBAJ|title=Echinoderms Through Time|last2=Guille|first2=Alain|last3=Feral|first3=Jean-Pierre|date=2020-12-17|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-000-12367-8|language=en}}</ref> Downey discovered several new species of sea stars, notably the deep-water ''[[Midgardia xandaros]]'', which was confirmed as the world's biggest starfish.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Downey|first=Maureen E.|date=1971|title=A New Starfish from the Gulf of Mexico|url=https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=File:Proceedings_of_the_Biological_Society_of_Washington_(IA_proceedingsofbi841971biol).pdf|journal=Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington|volume=84}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Midgardia xandaros Downey, 1972|url=http://www.marinespecies.org/aphia.php?p=taxdetails&id=178260|access-date=2021-05-03|website=World Register of Marine Species}}</ref> In 1992, she published the book ''Starfishes of the Atlantic''. Co-written with [[Ailsa McGown Clark]], it became a classic of the field.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Starfishes of the Atlantic / Ailsa M. Clark, Maureen E. Downey|url=https://www.si.edu/object/siris_sil_425881|access-date=2021-05-03|website=Smithsonian Institution|language=en}}</ref>

She retired in 1987 to [[San Juan Island]], where she lived until her death in 2000 at age 79.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

== Publications ==

* 1967 - ''Astronebris tatafilius'' (Euryalae: Asteronychidae), a new genus and species of Ophiuroid from the Aleutians, with a revised key to the family Asteronychidae. ''Proceedings of The Biological Society of Washington'' '''80''': 41–45. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34589376 BHL]
* 1968 - A note on the Atlantic species of the starfish genus ''Linckia''. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''81''': 41–44. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34605582 BHL]
* 1968 - Catalog of recent Echinoid type specimens in the U.S. National Museum Smithsonian Institution and the Museum of Comparative Zoology Harvard University. ''Bulletin of the United States National Museum'' '''264''': 1-99. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/7861337 BHL]
* 1969 - Catalog of recent Ophiuroid type specimens in major collections in the United States. ''Bulletin of the United States National Museum'' '''293''': 1–239. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/7881728 BHL]
* 1970 - Zorocallida, New Order, and ''Doraster constellatus'', New Genus and Species, with Notes on the Zoroasteridae (Echinodermata; Asteroidea). ''Smithsonian contributions to Zoology'' '''64''': 1–18. [https://repository.si.edu/handle/10088/5507 SI-repository]
* 1970 - ''Drachmaster bullisi'' new genus and species of Ophidiasteridae (Echinodermata, Asteroidea), with a key to the Caribbean species of the family. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''83'''(6): 77–82. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34572691 BHL]
* 1970 - ''Marsipaster acicula'', new species (Asteroidea: Echinodermata), from the Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''83'''(28): 309–312. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34572947 BHL]
* 1971 - A new species of the genus ''Solaster'' (Echinodermata: Asteroidea). ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''84'''(4): 39–42. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34563079 BHL]
* 1971 - Two new species of the genus ''Tamaria'' (Echinodermata: Asteroidea) from the Tropical Western Atlantic. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''84'''(5): 43–50. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34563083 BHL]
* 1971 - ''Ampheraster alaminos'', a new species of the family Asteriidae (Echinodermata: Asteroidea) from the Gulf of Mexico. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''84'''(6): 51–54. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34563091 BHL]
* 1972 - ''Midgardia xandaros'' new genus, new species, a large brisingid starfish from the Gulf of Mexico. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''84'''(48): 421–426. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34563503 BHL]
* 1973 - Starfishes from the Caribbean and the Gulf of Mexico. ''Smithsonian contributions to Zoology'' '''126''': 1–158. [https://repository.si.edu/handle/10088/5506 SI-repository]
* 1975 - Asteroidea from Malpelo Island with a description of a new species of the genus ''Tamaria''. in: {{aut|Graham, J.B.}}. The biological investigation of Malpelo Island, Colombia. ''Smithsonian contributions to Zoology'' '''176''': 86–90. [https://repository.si.edu/handle/10088/5254 SI-repository]
* 1977 - with {{Interlanguage link|Enrico Tortonese|it}}. On the genera ''Echinaster'' Mueller and Troschel, and ''Othilia'' Gray, and the validity of ''Verrillaster'' Downey. (Echinodermata: Asteroidea). ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''90'''(4): 829–830. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/39058595 BHL]
* 1979 - ''Pythonaster pacificus'' n.sp. a new starfish of the family Myxasteridae (Echinodermata: Asteroidea). ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''92'''(1): 70–74. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/35513777 BHL]
* 1979 - ''Hymenaster kieri'', a new species of starfish of the family Pterasteridae (Echinodermata: Asteroidea). ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''92'''(4): 801–803. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/35514522 BHL]
* 1980 - ''Floriaster maya'', new genus and species of the family Goniasteridae. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''93'''(2): 346–349. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34558120 BHL]
* 1981 - A new goniasterid seastar, ''Evoplosoma scorpio'' (Echinodermata: Asteroidea), from the northeastern Atlantic. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''94'''(2): 561–563. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34608418 BHL]
* 1982 - ''Evoplosoma virgo'', a new goniasterid starfish (Echinodermata: Asteroidea) from the Gulf of Mexico. ''Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington'' '''95'''(4): 772–773. [http://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/34965090 BHL]
* 1986 - Revision of the Atlantic Brisingida (Echinodermata: Asteroidea), with description of a new genus and family. ''Smithsonian contributions to Zoology'' '''435''': 1-57. [https://repository.si.edu/handle/10088/5505 SI-repository]
* 1992 - with [[Ailsa McGown Clark]]. Starfishes of the Atlantic.
